summary: Installed a GitHub-backed, privacy-safe agent coordination channel: exact leased status artifacts, typed heartbeat/blocker codes, a lane-side publisher, read-only report watcher with stale detection, a canonical agent bootstrap pack, and a deterministic no-model coordination observer. The status contract cannot persist arbitrary report text, and legacy boards without a status lease remain valid but cannot publish one.

pre_change_proof.evidence: Applied changed governance tests to the pinned base; the pre-change tree lacks the new agent-status module and the focused command fails before the implementation exists. The trusted acceptance runner replays this proof against the pinned base.

post_change_proof.evidence: Exact tested SHA passed 25 focused governance tests, including typed-only status persistence, free-text CLI rejection without echo, stale detection, and ignored Looper workspace coverage.
Candidate board passed schema, scoped status-lease, ownership, dependency, and acceptance validation.
Whitespace and conflict-marker check passed from the pinned task base through the exact tested SHA.

adversarial_review.goal: Find free-text persistence, private-data echo, stale-status bypass, scope escape, passive-watcher impersonation, raw loop-workspace retention, or a weakened check in the exact CTRL-002 chain.

open_risks.description: The Git watcher is deliberately read-only and cannot wake a remote LLM. Each remote host still needs an explicit authenticated runner to consume watcher events and publish a typed acknowledgement.
The current private-repository plan cannot enforce required checks or CODEOWNERS; codex-main remains the sole merger.
Agent and reviewer IDs are routing labels; GitHub actor separation or signing is required for cryptographic identity isolation.
CTRL-002 is coordination-only and does not repair the known product regression baseline.
